mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase above 5.0% signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% each month indicate broad demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: When HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5%, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0) signals supply chain disruptions and rising input costs, reducing corporate margins and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is below 105.0, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high residential construction permits (HOUST > 1100.0) indicate strong housing market activity, boosting consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 1100.0.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly core inflation rate increase above 0.3% (CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.3%) signals persistent inflation, prompting monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 0.3%, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and increases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2% and 0.2pp respectively indicate labor market contraction, reducing consumer demand and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines > 0.2% and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: When PAYEMS declines > 0.2% and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 450,000) indicates robust demand for goods and services, boosting corporate revenues and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS exceeds 450,000, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.
